simple.meaning: נָחָשׁ (nâchâsh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a snake (from its hiss).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 31 times across Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, 2 Kings, and 8 more, beginning at Genesis 3:1. Its meaning is built by comparing the passages where Scripture uses it.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נָחָשׁ (H5175).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: נָחָשׁ (nâchâsh) / H5175 is traced through Genesis 3:1, Genesis 3:2, Genesis 3:4, Genesis 3:13 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H5175. nachash I. נָחָשׁ noun masculine Gen 3:1 serpent (Late Hebrew id.; Arabic serpent, viper (Lane 406anything hunted ) is compare by Lag M, i, 230 ; BN 50, 188 Ba Es 48 , but improbable; Arabic see below [ נָחַשׁ below; on formation compare Lag BN 50 ); — absolute ׳נ Amos 5:19 +; construct נְחַשׁ Num 21:9 2 t.; plural נְחָשִׁים 21:6 ; Jer 8:17 ; — 1 serpent: a. as biting , Amos 5:19 ; Eccl 10:8 , in spite of charm ( לַחַשׁ ) 10:11 [compare Ecculs 12:13 ], Jer 8:17 (+ צִפְעֹנִים ; figurative of enemies); so הַשְׁרָפִים הַנְּחָשִׁים Num 21:6 (deadly; J E; compare Jacob Arab. Dicht. iv. 10 ff. ), and singular 21:9 , also (collective) 21:7 compare ׳נ שָׂרָף Deut 8:15 (+ עַקְרָב ); ׳נ figurative of oppressor, מְעוֺפֵף שָׂרָף וּפִרְיוֺ צֶפַע יֵצֵא נָחָשׁ מִשֹּׁרֶשׁ Isa 14:29 ; figurative of Dan Gen 49:17 (poem in J; || שְׁפִיפֹן ); נ ׳הֲמַת Psa 58:5 (simile of perniciousness of ungodly), compare ׳נ 140:4 ; simile of effect of wine Proverbs 22:32 (|| צִפִעֹנִי ). b. rod becomes ׳נ Exod 4:3 (J), compare 7:15 (E); נ דֶּרֶךְ צוּר ׳עֲלֵי Prov 30:19 . c. ׳נ (apparently) as hissing Jer 46:22 (in simile, compare Gie); as eating dust Isa 65:25 compare Micah 7:17 (in simile; see also Gen 3:14 ). d. as crafty tempter Gen 3:1-2 , 4 , 13 , 14 . 2 ׳נ (הַ)נְּחשֶׁת , bronze image of serpent Num 21:9 (twice in verse); 2Kin 18:4 (compare נְחֻשְׁתָּן ). 3 mythological ׳נ בָּרִחַ Job 26:13 fleeing serpent , of eclipse-dragon (compare לִנְיָתָן 3:6 ); also נ ׳לִוְיָתָן עֲקַלָּתוֺן נ ׳לִוְיָתָן ֗֗֗ בּרִחַ Isa 27:1 (symbolic of world-powers); ׳נ of sea-monster Amos 9:3 . — ׳נ with verb נָשַׁךְ bite Num 21:6 8 t. On supernatural character of serpents in Arabic belief see Nö Zeitschr. Für Völkerpsychol. i.(1860), 412-416 RS Kinship 197, Semitic i. 421 f. , 2d ed, 442 We Skizzen iii.147, Arab. Heid. 2, 152 f.
